relations.rationale: As head judge, Jun likely leads and sets the pace for the group.
Being the head judge has no bearing on weather conditions later in the day.
Dara arriving late after jogging explains why she was out of breath, so this supports the claim.
Dara's arrival time has no relation to Eli's height.
Dara's late arrival has no bearing on who brought the first-aid kit.
Dara arriving after Esme doesn't determine whether Jun arrived last, since it's about a different person's timing.
Dara's late arrival in the morning has no bearing on the evening tent setup.
Dara being out of breath from jogging has nothing to do with Eli's height.
Dara's breathlessness from jogging is unrelated to Jun's wrong turn.
Dara's morning breathlessness has no bearing on the midday lunch stop.
Dara's physical state has no bearing on how many teams existed.
Dara's morning breathlessness is unrelated to the group's readiness to rest later.
Eli being taller than most directly supports the claim that his height was useful for spotting distant markers.
Eli's height has no bearing on the group's readiness to rest.
Eli's usefulness for spotting markers doesn't indicate anything about team assignments.
Eli's height-based usefulness has no bearing on clouds gathering later.
Yara bringing the first-aid kit is unrelated to the group stopping at a stream to refill water.
Jun taking a wrong turn could explain why he arrived last, supporting the claim.
If Jun arrived last, this is compatible with him still making it before the group set off, supporting rather than contradicting.
Jun arriving last in the morning has no bearing on the group's overall tiredness and satisfaction by day's end.
